scope: Full original inspection grain-wheat01/02/03 and woman-childbirth01.
globalConditions: Technical acceptance is not owner approval or browser verification.
Botanical growth is illustrative and must not be presented as literal biological death causing germination.

entries.alt: A single intact golden wheat kernel rests on a pale stone in sunlight.
entries.caption: One grain rests alone. Jesus begins His comparison with the solitary grain before speaking of the fruitfulness connected with His approaching death.
entries.findings: Natural kernel crease, brush hairs and continuous surface; stone texture, scale of macro view and shadow are coherent. Distinct intact grain stage, no germination or harvest.
conditions: The resting place is illustrative; John12:24 does not specify a stone.
Technical acceptance is not owner approval or browser verification.

entries.recommendedTitle: A grain falls toward the soil
entries.alt: A hand releases one wheat kernel above a shallow furrow in dark soil.
entries.caption: A grain falls from an open pinch toward the earth. This simple planting moment accompanies Jesus' words about the grain that falls into the ground.
entries.findings: Thumb/index release, curled background fingers and sleeve coherent; single kernel is separate and airborne directly above furrow, plausible scale and gravity. Does not visually show death or completed germination.
conditions: The hand and furrow are illustrative, not a recorded agricultural action performed by Jesus.
Technical acceptance is not owner approval or browser verification.

entries.alt: A split grain rests in soil with a white root extending left and a green shoot rising at the opposite end.
entries.caption: A small root and shoot emerge from a grain in the soil. This early growth accompanies Jesus' comparison of a solitary grain with the fruitfulness He connects to His approaching death.
entries.findings: Revision required: root and shoot appear at opposite kernel ends and the kernel opens longitudinally into a bean-like pair. Wheat radicle and coleoptile arise from the embryo region; this image does not convincingly show coherent wheat germination. Texture and lighting pass, botanical structure does not.
conditions: Regenerate with largely intact elongated wheat grain; one basal embryo region visibly gives rise to a pale root curving downward and short coleoptile rising. No two cotyledon halves or root at distal brush end.
Technical acceptance is not owner approval or browser verification.

entries.alt: A pregnant woman reclines in a teal dress with her eyes nearly closed, holding the hand of an older woman beside her.
entries.caption: A woman in labor receives steady support through her pain. Jesus acknowledges the anguish of childbirth in the comparison He gives His disciples before speaking of joy.
entries.findings: Dignified fully clothed adult; believable strained facial expression, natural perspiration, grasped hands and resting hand on abdomen. Older attendant directs attentive gaze to mother. Closed eyes fit pain and concentration; no literal Christ appears. No exposed birth anatomy or invented emergency.
conditions: Unnamed illustrative mother and helper, not Mary or the Nativity; do not promise that every pregnancy ends safely or every sorrow quickly resolves.
Technical acceptance is not owner approval or browser verification.
